name: Kungseken, Knappfors

location.address: By the old lock (slussen), Knappfors bruksmiljö, Lunnedet nature reserve, Karlskoga municipality

access: Free. Stands in the open, fenced heritage area by the historic Knappfors ironworks lock, inside the Lunnedet nature reserve (established 1987, 188 ha, with camping and beaches); the site carries a public interpretive sign next to the tree, consistent with a place the public is meant to visit.
transport: No useful public transport found. Roughly 10km by road from central Karlskoga; reachable by car or bicycle via the Knappfors/Lunnedet road. If a future pass finds a rural bus route, correct this.
verify_notes: ALIVE, confirmed with high confidence: downloaded and viewed Commons file 'Knappfors_2024-07-22_image04.jpg' (CC BY-SA 4.0, Håkan Skogsjö) directly. It shows a large, clearly living oak in full summer leaf, its split/hollow lower trunk held together with visible metal support bands, standing inside a wooden fence in a mown meadow beside the old canal lock and a red-painted lock-keeper's building, with a small interpretive sign at its base. The file's own EXIF GPS (59°24'13.15"N, 14°25'21.6"E = 59.403653, 14.422668) matches the candidate coordinate almost to the metre, which is as confirmed as a pin gets. Two independent sv.wikipedia articles (on Knappfors itself and on the surrounding Lunnedet nature reserve) both separately name and place the tree. Also documented far back: a 1940s photo exists at Örebro Stadsarkiv/DigitaltMuseum ('Kungseken i Knappfors i Karlskoga, 1940-tal', site 403-blocked automated access, not opened) and an 1895 photo is referenced elsewhere, so this is a long-photographed, continuously standing tree, not a recent rediscovery. SPECIES: sources call it only 'ek' (oak) and give no scientific name; kept as genus-only per this file's existing convention for other 'Kungseken' entries, flagged for the reader. AGE/GIRTH: not documented in any source found within the time-boxed search; left blank rather than guessed, per policy. HISTORY/LEGEND: per sv.wikipedia, tradition holds that Gustav Vasa's sons, the future dukes (and kings) Johan and Karl, met at this oak by the Knappfors lock to conspire against their brother, King Erik XIV -- both Wikipedia articles independently flag this as 'a likely invented legend' rather than settled history, which the page should say plainly rather than presenting as fact. Knappfors itself is a preserved 19th-century ironworks/canal site (lock completed 1852) for floating pig iron from the Karlskoga and Nora mining districts. DESTINATION TEST, my own read: this is genuinely NOT near any published Swedish city (nearest is rural Karlskoga/Filipstad, neither on our map) so it is a real candidate for the 2026-08-31 single-famous-tree exception rather than a city addition. The case is moderate rather than clear-cut: real royal legend plus a visibly striking, well-tended veteran tree at a public heritage site with its own path and sign, but modest online fame (no dedicated Wikipedia article of its own, only mentioned inside two others, and I found no age/girth/species data anywhere) and no realistic public transport, so a page would have to be honest that this is a car trip to a small heritage site rather than a walk. Comparable in shape to Trogareds ek, already 'held' in this same leads file for a similar weak-destination read; unlike Trogareds ek, this one has excellent photographic and locational certainty.
